Awesome self-hosted tools

A curated list of small self-hosted services that are pleasant to run on a single machine. Every entry is maintained, documented, and has a working release in the last year.

Entries are grouped by what they help you do. Descriptions are intentionally short so the list stays readable on a phone.

Notes and sync

  • Noteshelf — plain-text notes with full-text search, file attachments, and a web clipper that works offline.
  • Syncpad — conflict-free collaborative documents built on CRDTs, with an optional read-only share link.
  • Journald — daily journaling with calendar navigation, export to markdown, and end-to-end encrypted backups.
  • Bookmarks — a fast bookmark manager with tags, full-page snapshots, and a reading queue.

Media and photos

  • Filmvault — indexes your movie collection, fetches posters from public databases, and streams to any browser.
  • Photonest — photo library with face grouping, map view, and automatic thumbnail generation for large collections.
  • Podcatcher — subscription-based podcast server that syncs progress across devices and removes old episodes.
  • Radiodial — internet radio directory with scheduled recordings and a simple web player.

Operations

  • Uptimebox — monitors HTTP endpoints and TCP ports from several locations and pages you when a check fails.
  • Backupd — incremental backups to local disks or S3-compatible storage, with restore verification after every run.
  • Logpond — structured log collection with a query language, alert rules, and retention policies per stream.
  • Secretshelf — team secret store with audit logs, per-environment access rules, and a CLI for CI jobs.

Contributing

Read the contribution guide before opening a pull request. Entries must include a link and a one-sentence description, and dead projects are removed without notice.

Sponsors

This list is sponsored by Acme Cloud and Northwind Hosting, both of which offer generous free tiers for open source projects.
